## Context / Problem
Homebrew users of `brew install navapbc/rebar/rebar` were left 2 releases behind because the tap `navapbc/homebrew-rebar` only bumps its formula from a scheduled workflow, and GitHub disables a scheduled workflow after 60 days with no repository activity.

## Observation
- navapbc/homebrew-rebar `.github/workflows/autobump.yml` (workflow id 316476444) was in state `disabled_inactivity` (checked 2026-11-09). Its last run was a scheduled run on 2026-10-28 23:31 PDT.
- `Formula/rebar.rb` still pointed at the nava_rebar-0.13.1 sdist, although 0.14.0 was published to PyPI on 2026-10-30. The runbook's claim that the 6-hourly schedule self-heals a missed release does not hold while the workflow is disabled.
- GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days with no repository activity. The tap only commits when a bump happens, so a gap of more than 60 days between releases disables it again.
- Operator remediation 2026-11-09: workflow re-enabled and dispatched; on 2026-11-18 its state is `active` and `Formula/rebar.rb` points at nava_rebar-0.16.0.tar.gz, matching PyPI.
- The tap workflow already accepts `workflow_dispatch: {}` (read from navapbc/homebrew-rebar `.github/workflows/autobump.yml` via `gh api`). The operator stored a classic `repo`-scope token as the navapbc/rebar Actions secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` (present in `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/secrets`) and chose the fix: rebar's release workflow triggers the tap's autobump directly.

## Approach
Add one job, `homebrew_tap`, to `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `needs: publish` and gated on `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` like the other post-publish jobs (`github_release`, `mcp_registry`). It has `permissions: {}` because it touches only the tap, through `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}`, and uses no actions (so nothing new to pin). One run step:
1. Waits (bounded, 30 x 10 s, the same shape as `mcp_registry`'s "Wait for PyPI to serve this version") until `https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/json` reports `info.version == inputs.version`, because the tap's script bumps only to PyPI's reported latest and would otherwise no-op on a stale CDN answer.
2. Reads the tap workflow's state with `gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/actions/workflows/autobump.yml --jq .state`. If it is `disabled_inactivity` it runs `gh workflow enable` (this is exactly the failure that left the tap behind); if it is `disabled_manually` it fails with an error rather than overriding a human's deliberate disable.
3. Runs `gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar --ref main`.
Dispatch from the release ties the bump to the release itself, so the tap no longer depends on its schedule staying alive; each bump commit also counts as tap activity. The new run step carries a `# mechanism-ok: ci_gate` marker naming this ticket, because the mechanism-delta ratchet counts every workflow run step (`scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py` `_detect_workflow_steps`).

docs/releasing.md step 3 ("Update the Homebrew tap") is rewritten: the release dispatches the autobump; the schedule remains as a backstop; the inactivity-disable failure mode, how the release job handles it, and the manual recovery (`gh workflow enable` + `gh workflow run`); and the stored `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` (classic, `repo` scope, copy in SSM `/rebar/prod/homebrew-tap-token`) replacing the "no stored cross-repo token" claim. The "Accounts / prerequisites" list gains the secret.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — new `homebrew_tap` job.
- `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py` — new structural test for the job.
- `docs/releasing.md` — step 3 and prerequisites.

## Testing
- New test `test_homebrew_tap_dispatch_job` in `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py`: the job exists, `needs` includes `publish`, `permissions` is empty, it is gated on `workflow_dispatch`, its env maps `GH_TOKEN` to `secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, and its run text contains `gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar` and the `disabled_manually` refusal. Written first and seen failing on the unmodified workflow.
- Failure path: the same test asserts the `disabled_manually` branch exits non-zero (the run text contains `exit 1` in that branch).
- `make lint` (zizmor on release.yml + actionlint) and `make verify` pass.
- Live check of the token, without cutting a release: one manual dispatch of the tap's autobump with the token read from SSM into a shell variable only (never printed or written), then the tap run's conclusion read back with `gh run list --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar --workflow autobump.yml`. It is a no-op bump when the formula already matches PyPI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] autobump.yml is enabled and Formula/rebar.rb points at the latest PyPI sdist.
      provenance: environment=github.com navapbc/homebrew-rebar; principal=JoeOakhartNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read via gh api of the workflow state and the formula contents
- [x] docs/releasing.md step 3 states the inactivity-disable failure mode and its recovery. Checked: reading the merged doc.
- [x] `.github/workflows/release.yml` has a `homebrew_tap` job that runs after `publish` and dispatches navapbc/homebrew-rebar `autobump.yml` with `secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`. Checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py` passes on merged main.
- [x] [non-codebase] The `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` token can dispatch the tap workflow.
      provenance: environment=github.com navapbc/homebrew-rebar; principal=HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN classic token (copy read from SSM /rebar/prod/homebrew-tap-token); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — one gh workflow run dispatch with the token, then the run's conclusion read back with gh run list
